parts.gloss: they will diminish / fall in stature
degrading deeds / actions that diminish one's stature
crab's eye seed (a tiny red seed)

literal: Even those who are like a hill will diminish, if they do degrading deeds that are like a tiny crab's eye seed.
translation: Even those whose stature is as great as a mountain will shrink in esteem if they commit a degrading act as tiny as a crab's eye seed.
modern: மலை போன்ற பெருமை உடையவர்களும், குன்றிமணி அளவு சிறியதான இழிவு தரும் செயல்களைச் செய்தால், தம் பெருமை அழிந்து தாழ்ந்து போவார்கள்.
explanation: This couplet emphasizes the absolute importance of maintaining one's honor and avoiding even the smallest dishonorable act. The poet uses a striking contrast between a massive hill ('kuṉṟu') and a tiny crab's eye seed ('kuṉṟi') to illustrate this. Even individuals of mountain-like greatness will lose their high standing and shrink in the eyes of the world if they commit a degrading deed, no matter how minuscule it may seem. The wordplay on 'kuṉṟu' (as a hill and as the verb to diminish) and 'kuṉṟi' (the tiny seed) reinforces how easily great honor can be eroded by a single small lapse.
